newsitem.title: UK: UPS says US to Europe traffic down 40 pct due to strike.
newsitem.headline: UPS says US to Europe traffic down 40 pct due to strike.

text.p: United Parcel Service said latest figures show traffic from the U.S. to Europe is down to 40 percent of normal levels as a result of the UPS Teamsters strike.
On Wednesday, the Teamsters union and UPS agreed to resume negotiations on Thursday to settle the four day old strike which has crippled the company.

Action by UPS pilots in support of the Teamsters has also grounded four aircraft in Europe, while two of its three daily transatlantic flights have been cancelled. Backup aircraft have been chartered for use within Europe under existing contingency plans.

A UPS spokeswoman told Reuters from Brussels that the overall situation within Europe remains is little different from earlier in the week with both domestic and intra-European services reporting business is unaffected.
The company says it handles some 700,000 packages daily in Europe with an export volume of 85,000 percent and 10.5 percent of the latter represents exports to the U.S.
A spokeswoman for Emery Worldwide said there has been a increase in customer demand from across the UK and Europe for premium product time-definite shipments to the U.S.
"This is especially so for next day and second day deliveries," she added.
"We'll do everything to help in such cases, especially if it involves our regular customers," she said.
But a Federal Express Corp spokewoman said that so far this week they have only had a small increase in enquiries about possible shipments.
